Special to Marijuananews
By Richard Cowan

December 7, 1999

I spoke today with Dr. Ethan Russo of the University of Montana, a leading researcher on the treatment of migraines.
See
Government Health Officials Deny Marijuana and Pain Study, Again -- NORML Press Release

Yesterday he was informed that NIDA's special review committee rejected his IRB-and FDA-approved protocol, and that he will not be permitted to purchase marijuana from NIDA for his study. The small amount involved – just 400 grams, less than a pound -- makes the refusal all the more absurd. Half of it would be placebo with the THC removed.

NIDA is the sole approved source for medical marijuana in DEAland. Consequently this highly politicized prohibitionist propaganda organization that funds 85% of the world’s "drug research" has an effective veto over any research on the medical use of cannabis.
See
Drug Czar Issues Statement On Marijuana For Medical Research:
"Such uses must only be part of clinical studies to expand the body of scientific understanding."
Helping the Patients Does Not Enter Into It.

Russo was told nothing about why the protocol was rejected and was also told he should expect to wait a month or longer before receiving any formal notification from NIDA. FDA gave its final approval to the study months ago.

This action will require a new protocol and a delay of at least six months.

The new HHS guidelines for medical marijuana research permit NIDA to create its own special review committee to review protocols that have already been approved by FDA and Institutional Review Boards.
See
HHS Announcement On New Medical Marijuana Research Rules
Shows It Is The Same Old Game.

This is not required for research on any other drug and is clearly designed to block research on medical marijuana.See
The Harsh Reality Of Clinical Trials
Shows Another Case of The Double Standard For Medical Marijuana.
The Context For "Research." -- 2 Articles

This action makes a mockery of the government’s claim that it wants to do research on medical marijuana. It also makes clear that making marijuana available for research was not the real motive for closing the so-called "Compassionate Use IND" to new patients.
See
The New York Times Reveals The New Medical Marijuana Research Policy
Is Just A Stalling Tactic That Will Do Nothing To Help Patients,
While The Washington Post Reveals That Frankly It Doesn’t Give A Damn.
– One and A Fraction Articles
